skill.name: ui-design-system
skill.description: Generate design system tokens, component guidance, responsive values, and developer handoff details for consistent UI work.
skill.summary: Create design tokens and UI system guidance from brand inputs.
skill.author: alirezarezvani

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited marketplace content describes a prior scanner match on the color value '#DC2626'. This is an error-state UI color token, not command-and-control terminology or behavior.
The cited content refers to 'self.base_unit = 8' and an '8pt grid system' for spacing. This is design-system terminology, not host or network reconnaissance.
The cited content discusses an 8pt spacing grid system. The word 'system' is used in the UI design sense and does not indicate reconnaissance.
Line 15 sets a base spacing unit with the comment '8pt grid system'. This is a static UI layout constant and performs no system inspection.
Line 22 uses markdown backticks to format a documented Python usage command. It is not executable Ruby or shell code inside the skill instructions.
Line 29 lists an '8pt spacing grid system' as a design feature. This is benign UI documentation and does not request system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose consistency when colors, spacing, and typography are defined by hand. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code generate clear design tokens and handoff guidance.
actual_capabilities: Generates color, typography, spacing, sizing, border, shadow, animation, breakpoint, and z-index tokens.
Creates design tokens from a brand color with modern, classic, or playful style presets.
Exports generated token sets in JSON, CSS, or SCSS formats through the included Python script.
Documents component system architecture, accessibility, responsive design, and developer handoff workflows.
Summarizes token categories and counts for quick review before exporting final values.
limitations: The generator uses preset style logic and does not replace a full brand design review.
Inputs are command-line arguments, so malformed colors may cause script errors.
It does not connect to Figma, design repositories, or external token registries.
Accessibility guidance still needs manual review against real product screens.

use_cases.title: Start a new design system
use_cases.description: Generate a first token set for colors, spacing, typography, shadows, and breakpoints from a brand color.

use_cases.title: Prepare developer handoff
use_cases.description: Export tokens in web-friendly formats and describe how components should use shared values.

use_cases.title: Standardize product UI
use_cases.description: Create consistent scales for teams that need shared design decisions across multiple product areas.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ui-design-system skill to generate a modern design token set for brand color #0066CC. Show a short summary of the token categories.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a default token system

prompt_templates.title: Export web tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate design tokens for brand color #3B82F6 with the playful style. Export them for a CSS project and explain where each token group should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Plan component usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a component guidance brief using the generated tokens for buttons, cards, forms, and navigation. Include accessibility notes for each component group.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for design and engineering alignment

prompt_templates.title: Audit a design system
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current token strategy against the ui-design-system guidance. Identify inconsistencies in color, spacing, typography, breakpoints, and developer handoff.

output_examples.input: Generate a modern token system for #0066CC.
output: A complete token set is generated for the brand color.
The result includes primary, secondary, neutral, semantic, and surface color groups.
It also includes typography, spacing, sizing, borders, shadows, animation, breakpoints, and z-index values.

output_examples.input: Prepare tokens for a frontend handoff.
output: The handoff includes export guidance for CSS or SCSS projects.
Developers receive named token groups for layout, type, color, elevation, motion, and responsive behavior.
Designers receive a summary they can compare with existing brand rules.
The skill can outline component architecture for shared UI patterns.
It can connect token choices to component states, spacing, and responsive behavior.
It can include accessibility reminders for contrast, focus states, and interaction targets.

best_practices: Start with the summary export so designers can review token coverage before implementation.
Use one style preset per product area to avoid mixed visual rules.
Validate generated colors and component states against accessibility requirements before release.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated tokens as final brand approval without design review.
Do not mix generated spacing scales with unrelated manual spacing values.
Do not skip developer handoff notes when exporting tokens for production use.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates design tokens for color, typography, spacing, sizing, borders, shadows, motion, breakpoints, and z-index values.

faq.question: Which export formats are supported?
faq.answer: The included generator supports JSON, CSS, and SCSS output formats.

faq.question: Can it create a complete brand system?
faq.answer: It can create a strong starting point, but brand strategy and visual approval still require human design review.

faq.question: Does it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: It includes accessibility guidance, but teams should still test contrast, focus states, and screen behavior in real interfaces.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is useful for UI designers, frontend developers, and design system leads who need shared token guidance.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The listed capability is a local Python token generator and supporting design-system instructions.
